description: A tool a workflow installs with `go install module@vN` is a pinned dependency that no manager reads. Renovate's gomod manager looks at go.mod; github-actions looks at `uses:`; a version inside a `run:` block is seen by neither, so it is a pin that will never be offered an update.

Measured here on 2026-10-31, which is why this organisation now carries the rule: gitsafe's own ci.yml pins `github.com/go-fleettools/fleettools/cmd/vulngate@v0.20.1` in its `govulncheck, judged by vulngate` step, while that module had reached v0.56.0 — thirty-six minor versions, and nothing said so. The step whose whole job is to decide what a vulnerability finding means was judging with a year-old judge, in the organisation that guards the credential.

depName is the MODULE, not the package: `go install` takes a package path and the proxy knows modules. The `/cmd/<name>` group is OPTIONAL because not every tool has its main package under cmd/ — go-fleettools/prwait and staletools have theirs at the module root, and `go install github.com/go-fleettools/prwait@v0.2.1` is how they are installed. Both shapes were measured against this expression when it was first written: `…/cmd/vulngate@v0.20.1` gives `fleettools`, `…/prwait@v0.2.1` gives `prwait`. A module whose own path ended in `/cmd/<something>` would still be read wrong; none does here.

A version of `latest` is deliberately NOT matched: there is no version to compare or rewrite. `go install golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@latest` in these lanes is a deliberate float, not an oversight.

The third copy of this manager, after go-fleettools/.github and go-crdt/.github. Two copies of a rule is one copy being wrong, and the alternative — a shared preset repository — is a dependency every organisation's Renovate run must fetch before it can read its own config. Kept as copies deliberately, and every copy's description says so.

One pull request per repository for everything non-breaking, rather than one per dependency. Merging them singly means every merge rebases the others and restarts their checks: one run over an organisation of 34 repositories updated 109 branches and merged 2. Grouped, a repository needs one round of checks instead of dozens.

Never auto-merge the Go toolchain, and never let it ride in somebody else's group. A rule that says automerge:false for one dependency is defeated by grouping, because Renovate decides automerge per BRANCH: go 1.27.0 rode into seven repositories inside a branch called renovate/github-actions, whose other dependency was actions/setup-go. Ungrouped, it gets a branch of its own and this setting governs it. It matters because go1.27.0 miscompiles on loong64 (golang/go#81000, bisected on real hardware to 3fdac6780b): go-gfx/gfx fails that lane and stayed open only because the lane failed, which is the CI gate holding rather than this rule. A repository without such a lane sees nothing.
